issue_context.title: [BUG] SharedArrayBuffer should work in WebKit
issue_context.body: This popped up in https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/13976, SharedArrayBuffer was reenabled in Safari https://webkit.org/blog/12140/new-webkit-features-in-safari-15-2/ but we disabled COOP handling in https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/9185 as it broke some other functionality in WebKit. We should reenable COOP to match Safari and make SharedArrayBuffer work.
comments:
Hi all, thanks for the great tool. 

Why has this issue stopped for almost half a year? I don't think there is a major barrier since the fix is to undo one line, making it behave the same as the current real Safari.

My problem is not with `SharedArrayBuffer` but with `performance.now`; however, I think that the root cause is the same and lies in this issue.

Since developing a cross-browser JS library, I have been using Playwright and `performance.now` to detect performance degradation with all multiple engines. (This is not a serious performance measurement but a part of CI.) However, the time resolution is currently fixed at 1 second with plain Playwright. Then I have been waiting several months, with almost no possibility of checking for degradation with WebKit.

I have confirmed the problem was mitigated by the proper use of COOP/COEP on two other engines. I wish to be corrected to the same status as the others.

After a while, I realized that my measurement approach was fundamentally wrong.

I had called `performance.now()` within `page.evaluate(() => {...})`. But as a policy, to begin with, I think it was a mistake to make the accuracy of the data dependent on the observed objects. The responsibility should be on the observer, i.e., my code on the Node.js/Playwright side.

Through some trial and error, my problem is solved because I have found several ways independent of the browser's time resolution. Therefore, I am no longer in a hurry about this issue.

In any case, I think it is not desirable to behave differently from plain Safari, so I would appreciate it if you continued to consider fixing this problem.

A while ago, I realized I was fundamentally wrong about another thing. Not only had I checked the behavior at hand, but I also believed that the patch in browser_patches/webkit was up to date when I wrote [my first comment here](#issuecomment-1287827659) .

That was a mistake. The browser patch has been closed/proprietary since last August. #16845 #17556

Here is what I want to believe next.
> "Microsoft loves open source"
> Judge us by the actions we have taken in the recent past, our actions today and in the future
https://pulse.microsoft.com/nl-nl/transform-nl-nl/na/fa1-microsoft-loves-open-source/
